answer_verbatim:
Finding the right dental practice for an implant in Dallas depends heavily on your budget, whether you need tooth extractions or bone grafting first, and how anxious you are about the procedure. 

Dental implants are surgical procedures involving both a **surgeon** (who places the metal post into the jawbone) and a **restorative dentist** (who puts the visible crown on top). Some practices have specialists under one roof, while others require you to go to an oral surgeon for the post and your general dentist for the crown.

Here are specific, highly-rated dental practices in the Dallas area to call, categorized by what they do best:

---

### 1. For High-End, Comprehensive Care (Best for Complex Cases)
If you have multiple missing teeth, bone loss, or want the absolute highest level of technology and specialized care under one roof, look here:

*   **Dallas Dental Arts** 
    *   **Why call them:** They are known for advanced cosmetic and restorative dentistry, including full-mouth rehabilitation and implants. They use state-of-the-art 3D imaging to plan implant placement precisely.
    *   **Best for:** Patients who want a boutique experience and have high aesthetic standards for the final crown.
*   **Park Cities Dental Group** 
    *   **Why call them:** Located in a premier Dallas neighborhood, this team handles both the surgical and restorative phases of implants. They have a reputation for meticulous work and patient comfort.
    *   **Best for:** Patients living in North Dallas/Park Cities looking for comprehensive, high-end care.

### 2. Dedicated Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (Best for the Surgical Phase)
If your general dentist told you that you need bone grafting, sinus lifts, or have complicated dental anatomy, you should start with a dedicated surgical practice. (Note: You will still need to return to your general dentist for the crown afterward, though these surgeons coordinate closely).

*   **North Texas Dental Surgery (Dr. Tamir Sweidon / Associates)**
    *   **Why call them:** Highly respected oral and maxillofacial surgeons in the Dallas area specializing in dental implants, wisdom teeth, and corrective jaw surgery. 
    *   **Best for:** Patients who need complex bone grafting or want IV sedation during the procedure.
*   **DFW Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery**
    *   **Why call them:** They have multiple locations around the metroplex and are experts in computer-guided implant surgery, making the procedure faster and less invasive.

### 3. For "Teeth in a Day" / Full-Arch Replacements
If you are missing most or all of your teeth and are looking at All-on-4 or full-mouth restorations:

*   **Nuvia Dental Implant Center (Dallas/Fort Worth location)**
    *   **Why call them:** Nuvia specializes exclusively in permanent, full-arch dental implants. Unlike traditional places that make you wear temporary dentures for months while the implant heals, Nuvia utilizes a specific technique that allows them to attach a permanent, durable set of teeth *days* after surgery.
    *   **Best for:** Patients looking for a complete smile overhaul who want to bypass temporary plastic dentures.

### 4. For Value & Efficiency (Corporate/High-Volume Centers)
If you are paying out of pocket and are concerned about cost, high-volume implant centers often have streamlined pricing and in-house financing.

*   **ClearChoice Dental Implant Center (Dallas)**
    *   **Why call them:** ClearChoice is a national brand with a dedicated Dallas office. They handle everything—consultation, 3D scans, surgery, lab work, and placement—all in one building. 
    *   **Best for:** Patients wanting a streamlined, assembly-line approach where the surgeons and the lab technicians talk to each other daily. (Be sure to get a second opinion on price, as they can sometimes lean toward expensive, full-arch recommendations).

---

### Questions You Must Ask When You Call Them:

When you call these offices for a consultation, do not just ask "How much is an implant?" (Since every mouth is different, they can't give an accurate quote over the phone). Instead, ask these four specific questions:

1.  **"Do you place the implant post *and* the crown here, or will I have to go to a separate doctor for part of the process?"** *(Knowing this helps you understand where you'll be driving and who you're paying).*
2.  **"Is the consultation fee applied toward the cost of the procedure?"** *(Many consultations cost $100–$300 out of pocket).*
3.  **"Does your quote include extractions, bone grafting, and the abutment, or are those separate fees?"** *(Unscrupulous offices sometimes quote you just for the metal screw, leaving out the parts required to actually finish the tooth).*
4.  **"What kind of sedation options do you offer?"** *(Ask this if you suffer from dental anxiety).*
